title: PostHog session recording not disabled on token-bearing resume page — sanitize_properties scrub covers events only
evidence:
<> "capture_pageview:true,capture_pageleave:true,"
<> "opt_out_capturing_by_default:true,"
// F3: the resume page's URL carries the 288-bit continue token — a
// read-capability for applicant PII. Scrub it (and the draft-erasure
// sibling) from every URL-ish event property before anything leaves
// the browser; the token must never land in the analytics store
...
<> "sanitize_properties:function(p){"  — and a repo-wide grep of server/src finds no `disable_session_recording` / `session_recording` config anywhere. form_pages.gleam:435 renders this snippet on the resume page (`form_view.view_posthog_snippet(vacancy.short_code, posthog_api_key)` inside view_resume_page).
detail: sanitize_properties only amends event properties; PostHog session recording (rrweb) is a separate pipeline it does not filter. If recordings are enabled in project settings, the /apply/:code/resume/<token> URL is captured in recording metadata, leaking the PII-read capability to the analytics store despite the event-property scrub.
recommended_fix: Add `disable_session_recording:true` to the posthog.init config in view_posthog_snippet (or an explicit session_recording mask config), closing the recording pipeline on the token-bearing resume page and the PII form generally.
